title: Unit – 5 : Session – 7 : SLO – 2  |  Implementation of MST — Kruskal's Algorithm
sections: I. Pseudocode Fill-in-the-Blanks
1. Sort all edges in ASCENDING (non-decreasing) order of weight.
2. Initialize parent array for all vertices (each vertex is its own parent).
3. Initialize MST as an empty set.
4. For each edge (u,v) in sorted order:
a. If find(u) != find(v): i. Add (u,v) to MST.  ii. Perform UNION operation.
5. Stop when MST has n-1 edges.
II. Complete the C Code Snippet
int findParent(int parent[], int i) {
if (parent[i] != i)
parent[i] = findParent(parent, parent[i]);   // Path compression
return parent[i];
III. Predict the Output
Edges sorted: A-B(2), B-C(3), A-C(4).
Accept A-B(2); accept B-C(3); A-C would form a cycle -> skip.
Total MST weight = 2 + 3 = 5.
IV. Identify Cycle Formation
No — A-C (3) must NOT be included. A and C are already connected through A-B-C,
so adding A-C would create the cycle A-B-C-A. Kruskal's accepts an edge only if find(u) != find(v).
V. Pseudocode Error Spot
Wrong: the snippet adds the edge when find(u) == find(v) — that ADDS a cycle.
Fix: if (find(u) != find(v)) { Add edge (u,v) to MST; Union(u, v); } else { Continue; }
VI. Creative Reasoning
Kruskal's is preferred for sparse graphs because its cost is dominated by sorting the edges, O(E log E),
and with few edges (E << V^2) this is far cheaper than Prim's O(V^2) array version; the Union-Find
structure also handles the disconnected forest gracefully without scanning whole rows of a matrix.
